saved.name: New generator proposal: classify, route, cost, price, accept
saved.prompt: Priya needs the Halden Biopharma proposal by Friday 6 November: six new waste streams from their Caldwell Bend plant, 4,860 tons a year from February 2027, three-year contract. Characterise and classify each stream, work out which of our units can take it under its permit, its capacity and Halden's destruction requirement, cost every route and price it from the price book, test the margin against the floor, and draft the acceptance memo, the quote letter and the pricing schedule in the Delmar structure. Attached: the six profiles and the Delmar pricing schedule.
steps: Characterise and classify the six streams
Check the network: permits, capacity and the fallback for each stream
Cost every route and price each stream from the book
Check acceptance and what has to be in place before the first shipment
Draft the acceptance memo, the quote letter and the pricing schedule

saved.name: Outlet loss: size, cause, options
saved.prompt: Keep every accepted stream with a permitted outlet that has capacity when it arrives, and keep every stream above the margin floor. Check each nightly load of profiles, manifests, bookings, outlet approvals and the price book; when a shipment loses its outlet, an approval runs out, or a stream falls under the floor, size it, look at what the rest of the network can take, and work out what can still be done before I ask.
steps: Confirm what the load flagged, and size it
Why it happened, and whether anyone is on it
Look across the network: headroom, holds, outlets, clauses
What can still be done, including nothing
Notice to the people you chose
